subject.title: [Bug]: Non-Anthropic models output tool calls as plain text '[tool: exec]' instead of tool_use blocks

question: When a tool-enabled provider emits only a bare `[tool: name]` marker with no structured call or arguments, should OpenClaw retry/fallback/block with a clear warning, or keep treating it as plain assistant text?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the safe behavior is product policy because execution is impossible without arguments and fallback/blocking changes provider compatibility.

options.title: Retry or fallback with warning
options.body: Detect bare registered-tool markers, avoid executing them, and route to retry/fallback or a clear user/operator warning for tool-dependent turns.

options.title: Document as unsupported
options.body: Keep the current parser boundary and document affected models as manual-only or tools-disabled when they emit bare markers.

options.title: Attempt text-to-tool recovery
options.body: Try a model-driven repair step to obtain arguments, accepting extra complexity and a higher safety review bar.

recommendation.title: Retry or fallback with warning
recommendation.body: Detect bare registered-tool markers, avoid executing them, and route to retry/fallback or a clear user/operator warning for tool-dependent turns.

likelyOwner.reason: This crosses core provider fallback policy and the current repair-package boundary, and CODEOWNERS plus recent refactor history make this the clearest routing owner.
